    Affiliate Content Studio

    Turns an Amazon product into ready-to-post Pinterest and Instagram videos with copy, then tracks what went out.

    • Claude decides, the backend executes. Claude Code runs headless, writes one validated result file and exits. A clean exit code isn't success; a valid file is.
    • Spend is checked before it happens. The estimate goes on screen for approval before any render, and every copy variant is measured against platform limits.
    • Compliance is code. Platform rules live in one module that feeds the prompt, the validator and the on-screen counters. Disclosures are added by the backend.
    • Outgrew n8n. It started as a workflow; when that hit its limits I rebuilt it as an app with a job queue, a worker and live log streaming.

    297 tests, 8 end-to-end suites

    Next.js 15, Prisma, SQLite, Auth.js, server-sent events, Claude Code, Higgsfield, FFmpeg, Zod

    Tapworth

    An NFC terminal sits between a shop's till and its receipt printer and reads every line item as it prints. That feeds a merchant dashboard, a receipt wallet with an AI agent, and a consent-gated identity score. I built all of it, firmware included.

    • Grounded after generation. Every figure the agent writes is checked against a tool result, and anything unsupported is deleted before the user sees it.
    • Guardrails in code, tested in CI. The user's tap creates agent memory, and sending anything is never automated at any autonomy level. About $0.021 per question.
    • Arabic right-to-left from day one, with automated English/Arabic parity checks, dark mode and a contrast auditor.
    • The till never depends on it. Firmware forwards every byte first, a normally closed relay keeps printing if the device dies, and TLS is pinned to the root certificate.

    575 backend tests, Docker, CI, structured logging

    Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Redis, vanilla JavaScript, ESP32-S3 firmware, Railway, Cloudflare

      Prawn, an AI voice receptionist

      Answers a restaurant's phone in natural speech: menu and allergen questions, plus booking, checking, changing and cancelling tables.

      • An agent with seven tools. Twilio calls reach an n8n workflow where an LLM agent handles each turn and ElevenLabs speaks the reply.
      • Menu answers come from the menu tool, never from the model's memory, so it can't invent dishes or prices.
      • Knows returning callers before the greeting plays, and texts a confirmation after every booking.
      • Built for real phone calls. Silence handling, goodbye detection, escalation to staff, a fallback voice if ElevenLabs is down, and every turn logged for scoring.

        Eatlo

        Table ordering for Indian restaurants. Every table gets an NFC and QR card; diners tap or scan, then order and track their food in the browser with no app.

        • Four interfaces, one backend: customer ordering, a real-time kitchen display, an owner dashboard and an operator console, over 120 API endpoints and 25 tables.
        • A new restaurant in 1.6 seconds. The provisioning CLI created the tenant, four tables, the owner account and the QR links in one run, 95 ms of it server time.
        • AI menu import read a menu photo into 12 items in 13 seconds with gpt-4o-mini, then waited for the owner to review before saving anything.
        • Built for Indian rules: veg and non-veg marks, CGST and SGST split on every bill, a scheduled discount engine, staff roles and rate limiting. I designed the physical table cards too.

        React, Vite, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Socket.io, JWT, Railway, Vercel

            AI OS

            My own multi-agent system: a planner, a task breakdown agent, research and outreach agents behind a LangGraph pipeline, with a dashboard and a human approval queue.

            • 20 agents behind one worker, 126 API routes and two LangGraph pipelines, with job status streaming to the dashboard through Redis.
            • Nothing is ever sent. Outreach lands in the queue as a draft, and the app has no send capability at all: its button only marks a row as sent.
            • The local model didn't get used, and the run says so. Ollama can't see the GPU on this machine, so Qwen 3 8B runs on the CPU and overruns the app's own 180-second timeout. The pipeline failed twice for real before I switched the demo to the app's LiteLLM routing and pointed it at Claude.
            • The capture caught real faults. The pipeline never records its approval pause, so it never reaches the queue page. That failed check is in the replay.

            This run: 4 model calls, 12,930 tokens in, 19,193 out, $0.118, 320 seconds

              Listing watcherPlaywright price and stock tracker that feeds n8n. Public, code includedBuilt
              • Watches product pages, extracts the fields named in a config file, and records what changed: price up or down, back in stock, gone. Changes go to an n8n webhook, signed and queued, so nothing is lost while n8n is down.
              • It notices when it breaks. If a selector matches nothing, or matches two things, it keeps the last known value, records the miss and marks the target unhealthy. Two misses in a row and the target leaves the rotation until a person looks at it. That's the difference between a scraper and one you can still run in six months.
              • It scrapes nobody to test itself. The repo ships a small fixture site and a script that breaks it on purpose, so the whole suite runs offline and gives the same answer every time.
              • Good manners are the design, not a setting. robots.txt is obeyed with no override flag, one request per domain at a time, no logins and no captchas. It extracts only the configured fields and fails loudly if a value looks like someone's email or phone number.
              • An optional Claude fallback proposes a new selector when one breaks. It's off by default and never edits the config on its own: proposals wait for approval.

              TypeScript, Playwright, Zod, n8n. Prices stored as integer minor units, never floats.

              ComfyUI thumbnail workflowProduct thumbnails where the product's own pixels surviveBuilt
              • The model never redraws the product. A generated version of a charger gets the ports wrong, and for affiliate content that's a lie. So it cuts the product out of the real photo, generates only the scene behind it, and composites the original back at full resolution. The client then checks every product pixel against the source and refuses to save the image if one differs by more than 1/255. Across every render made while building it, the maximum difference was 0.
              • One photo and a short brief produce a Pinterest pin, a square and a vertical frame, each with a contact shadow and optional headline.
              • Every image is written with a provenance file beside it: workflow hash, model, seed, sampler, steps, prompt and timings. The seed comes from the product id, so a rerun gives the same image unless the brief changed.
              • Two graphs ship: one using stock nodes only, so it runs after a clean ComfyUI install, and one using custom nodes for better lighting. A missing node gives a clear message instead of a stack trace.
              • A mock ComfyUI server replays recorded responses, so the client and every error path are tested in CI with no GPU and no model downloads.
              • Built to fit an 8 GB card, and it drops into Affiliate Content Studio as a render step beside Higgsfield.

              ComfyUI, TypeScript, SDXL-class models, Affiliate Content Studio. Measured on an RTX 4060: about 7–8 s per image warm, 4.33 GB peak VRAM. 101 test cases.

              Memory-guided red teaming of LLMsMSc dissertation, Aston University, supervised by Dr Sourav SahaIn progress
              • A pre-registered AI safety study: does a layered attack memory make an automated red-teamer better against text-only LLMs, and does the gain come from retrieval or just from having examples in context?
              • Three conditions (retrieval memory, no memory, and a length-matched sham memory of random past attacks), compared with campaign-level paired permutation tests.
              • An epsilon-greedy bandit per risk category against a locally hosted, 4-bit quantised Llama 3.1 8B, scored by a pinned GPT-4o judge. Every request comes verbatim from the StrongREJECT benchmark.
              • The pilot caught a template bug leaking category labels into attacks. I fixed it and filed the fix as a formal pre-registration amendment.

              502 passing tests. Python, Hugging Face Transformers, OpenAI API, pytest.

              Fast, not fragile

              How I work with AI coding tools, and the rules that show up in every project above.

              The agents type. I own the design.

              Claude Code and Cursor write most of the code. I own the architecture, the written contracts they work from, and the tests that decide when something is done.

              Model output is untrusted

              Anything a model returns is validated, repaired or discarded before it reaches a user or a live system.

              Rules that matter live in code

              Guardrails, legal disclosures and spending limits are enforced by code and covered by tests, not requested politely in a prompt.

              Pick the tool that fits

              Visual workflows are great for integration. When a pipeline outgrows them, I rebuild it as an app instead of forcing it.

              Things that broke, and what I did

              Shipping solo means hosting, DNS and servers are mine too.

              What brokeWhat I did
              Company email failed validationMoved tapworth.co.uk to Cloudflare, set up MX, SPF and DKIM, merged two SPF records into one, and kept mail records unproxied.
              Custom domains didn't resolvePointed GoDaddy domains at Vercel with A and CNAME records and saw them through propagation.
              A monorepo wouldn't buildFixed a Railway build-plan failure by setting the service root directory, then sorted internal versus public database URLs and migrations on deploy.
              Logins failed between two hostsTraced failures between a Vercel frontend and a Railway API to the CORS origin setting.
              Merchants got duplicate emailsTwo workers ran the same scheduled job, so I added a Redis distributed lock.
              Devices would break on certificate rotationPinned firmware TLS to the root certificate so terminals keep connecting when 90-day leaf certificates rotate.
              Two command-line tools clashedUntangled a Windows PATH conflict between two different CLIs both named hf.
